meta.title: Get Started · Aethyr docs
meta.description: Install Aethyr, connect your AI assistant over MCP, and make your first Blueprint edit by asking.

article.heading: Speak Blueprint.
article.lead: Aethyr is an MCP server that lets your AI assistant read and author Unreal Engine 5 Blueprints in plain language. This page gets you from zero to your first AI-made edit in about five minutes.
article.audNote: Both of you are covered: beginner steps are spelled out; the deeper "how it works" notes are marked for the vets.

sections.heading: What it actually is
sections.html:
Two pieces that travel together:

  • A UE editor plugin that knows how to introspect and safely mutate Blueprint assets.
  • A standalone MCP server (AethyrMcp) that speaks the Model Context Protocol, so AI clients can drive that plugin by talking to it: no Python, no editor scripting, no C++.

Every build ships the full tool surface. Reads can't mutate anything. Writes compile the Blueprint and back up each asset before its first save, and a batch rolls back if its compile fails.

sections.heading: 5-minute quickstart
sections.html:
◈ Acquire the pluginAethyr for Unreal Engine 5UE 5.8+server precompiledno telemetry↓Downloadlatest release
  1. Get the plugin. Pick a zip on the download page and unzip it into your project's Plugins/ folder. The precompiled zip drops straight in on UE 5.8. The source zip needs one build step first.
  2. Run setup. AethyrMcp.exe setup --project <YourProject> (or ask your AI to "get Aethyr from aethyr.gg") registers the server with the AI clients you have installed, at user scope, with full read and write access. One entry follows whichever project you open your AI client in. Set AETHYR_PROJECT only if you want to pin one project.
  3. Restart your AI client.
  4. Get the samples (optional). Ask your AI to "install the Aethyr samples". It builds sample Blueprints, data, materials and UI into /Game/AethyrSamples for the tutorials, and it never overwrites your own assets.
  5. Ask it something. Try: "List the Blueprints under /Game and tell me what BP_PlayerCharacter does."

That's the whole loop. From here, everything is just asking for what you want. See the user-story tutorials.

sections.heading: Connect your AI
sections.html:
AethyrMcp.exe setup registers Aethyr for you. Aethyr is a standard MCP stdio server, so if you'd rather add it by hand, this is the manual fallback.

Claude / any MCP client

// mcpServers block (~/.claude.json for Claude Code, claude_desktop_config.json for Claude Desktop)
{
  “mcpServers”: {
    “aethyr”: {
      “command”: “C:/Path/To/AethyrMcp.exe”,
      “env”: {
        “AETHYR_BACKEND”: “auto”
      }
    }
  }
}

Writes are on by default in every build. Add AETHYR_READ_ONLY=1 to the env block for a session that can't change anything. Run AethyrMcp.exe config --client=<name> to print this block with your own paths filled in. It prints the pinned form.

VS Code and Visual Studio use servers with "type": "stdio", and Codex uses TOML ([mcp_servers.aethyr]). Set AETHYR_PROJECT for Claude Desktop and Windsurf. Add AETHYR_ENGINE_DIR only if doctor can't find the engine.

Vet The backend is auto by default: it probes per call and routes to a live editor if one's open (over a local socket), or spins a headless editor when it isn't. You never pick a backend by hand.

sections.heading: Skills & the audit agent
sections.html:
The plugin ships skills and an agent that teach your AI how to use the tools well. setup installs them into your user profile for the AI clients you use: ~/.agents/skills/aethyr-* for Copilot CLI, VS Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and Windsurf, and ~/.claude/skills/aethyr-* for Claude Code. The agent goes to each client that supports one. Nothing goes into your project.

  • aethyr-core: reading and the wire format.
  • aethyr-edit: writes and batches (apply_ops, preview_ops, compile_function).
  • aethyr-live: driving the running editor.
  • aethyr-triage: errors, recovery and updates.
  • aethyr-bp-audit: a read-only auditor. Ask it "audit /Game/AI" and it fans out reads and returns a tight report without touching anything.

Why this matters: the skills are what turn "call a tool" into "do the right sequence of tools." With them installed, your AI reaches for preview_ops before a risky batch, keys links on (node, pin), and explains a failure instead of flailing.

sections.heading: How it works (for the curious)
sections.html:
Vet A few load-bearing ideas:

  • Progressive disclosure. tools/list starts with a small core set plus meta-tools to keep token cost down. Your AI widens it with enable_tool_category, or calls any tool directly with call_tool.
  • Compile gate and backups. A batch compiles once before it saves, and a failed compile rolls the whole batch back. Single-step writes save as they go unless you set AETHYR_STRICT_COMPILE=1. Before the first save of an asset in a session, Aethyr copies it to a backup ring. Python scripts, config edits and bridged Epic writes skip these checks.
  • Atomic batches. apply_ops with atomic:true reverts every change in the batch if any step fails, so your asset is never left half-rewritten.
  • Package paths, not object paths. Everything addresses assets as /Game/AI/BP_Foo, never /Game/AI/BP_Foo.BP_Foo.

sections.heading: Aethyr & Epic's MCP
sections.html:
Unreal Engine 5.8 ships Epic's own MCP plugin, ModelContextProtocol. It's experimental at time of writing. Aethyr doesn't replace it. Aethyr turns Epic's server on for you and passes its tools through. Your AI connects to one server and gets both tool sets.

What each one covers

AreaEpic's MCPAethyr
Where it runsInside the editor process, over HTTP.A separate server process. A bad call can't take your editor down with it.
Editor neededYes. No editor, no tools.No. With no editor open, Aethyr starts a headless one for reads and writes.
Blueprint writesEdits graphs node by node through BlueprintTools, one call at a time.Node-level edits too, plus whole batches with a preview, a compile check before saving, and rollback.
Write safetyApplies each change directly.Compiles before saving, backs up each asset before its first save, and rolls a failed batch back.
Editor controlBroad: PIE, viewport, camera, selection, the Slate UI. It grows with each engine release.Reaches all of Epic's editor control through the bridge.
Other systemsToolset plugins for Niagara, Sequencer, GAS, UMG and more.Reaches those toolsets through the bridge.
SetupEnable the plugin. Its server doesn't start on its own by default.Nothing to do. Aethyr switches Epic's MCP and its toolsets on when the editor starts.

How the bridge works

  • Epic's server starts on its own. Aethyr's editor module starts Epic's server when the editor loads. Your .uproject and config files aren't touched.
  • Every project gets it on a normal launch. Once the editor has started, Aethyr's editor module switches on ModelContextProtocol and every Epic toolset whose own plugins are already on in your project. Nothing is written to your .uproject. The editor log's [Aethyr] Epic MCP mount lines say what it switched on, and what it left off and why.
  • Aethyr finds Epic's server. It dials 127.0.0.1:8000/mcp by default and follows a port you changed in Epic's project settings. AETHYR_EPIC_URL overrides both. doctor shows the address it picked.
  • Three tools reach everything. epic_list_toolsets lists what Epic has enabled, epic_describe_toolset shows one toolset's functions, and epic_call_tool runs one. Your AI can also turn on one tool per Epic function with enable_tool_category("epic").
  • Same rules as native tools. Aethyr sorts every Epic tool into read or write, and counts an unknown one as a write. A read-only session refuses bridged writes. Bridged calls also queue behind the same per-project lock, which keeps one from landing in the middle of another session's batch.

Which side handles what

You don't pick. The skills steer your AI to the right side. It mostly works out like this:

  • Aethyr's own tools: Blueprint graph authoring (add_node, wire_pins, compile_function, apply_ops), anything that has to work with no editor open, and any write that should be compile-checked and roll back as a unit.
  • Epic's tools, through the bridge: PIE, the viewport, camera and selection, driving the Slate UI, and authoring in Niagara, Sequencer, GAS and UMG.

Bridged writes skip Aethyr's safety net. Epic's editor applies them directly. They get no compile gate and no rollback. Have your AI read back what changed. Set AETHYR_EPIC_BACKUP=1 and pass target_asset to epic_call_tool to back the asset up first.

Vet The bridge needs a live editor. The headless editor never serves Epic's tools, since Epic's server lives inside a running UnrealEditor. A toolset that needs a plugin your project doesn't use stays off. To force one on, start the editor with AethyrMcp.exe launch-editor --epic-toolsets <Name>. Set AETHYR_EPIC_AUTOMOUNT=0 in the editor's environment to stop the mount. Set AETHYR_EPIC_INTEROP=0 to turn the bridge off. The reference has every flag.

Want the long version? Epic's MCP vs Aethyr lists every Epic toolset next to the matching Aethyr tool, and walks through how Aethyr handles Epic's rough edges.
